label: 2026-08-20 discriminating corpus — 58 memories, 26 queries, 10 synonym-only with lexical decoys
note:
NOT comparable to the 0.7902 scaffold baseline it replaces, and lower on purpose. The corpus changed, so this is a new instrument rather than a regression.

The scaffold had no synonymy and no decoys, so nearly everything scored well and every change to retrieval looked like an improvement — which is what EvalFixtures.isScaffold() exists to warn about. This corpus pairs each synonym-only query with a lexical decoy that shares the query's words, is semantically wrong, and is deliberately fresher and more accessed. BM25, recency and usage all point at the decoy; only a semantic model reaches the target. A low absolute number means the instrument discriminates.

What it measured on arrival: model and weights are multiplicative, not additive. gte-small at LEGACY weights buys +0.083 nDCG@10 overall but only +0.011 on synonym-only, because a semantic score is one vote of six against recency, usage, decay and importance. Relevance weights with no semantic model buy +0.069 and +0.004. Together they buy +0.156 and +0.063, and bge-small at relevance weights buys +0.100 on synonym-only — nine times what the model alone was worth. Neither half works without the other, and testing either alone makes the other look worthless.

correctly_empty_rate is 0.0 and that is a REAL GAP, not a property of the corpus: both should-return-nothing queries return something. Recorded at the measured value rather than aspirationally, so a future fix shows as an improvement — but it should be fixed. Note the history below: this metric was once baselined at 0.0 by accident and the test named after it could not fail for two months.

PRESERVED FROM THE PREVIOUS BASELINE, because the reasoning still binds:
  * MemoryDao.searchFts orders by decayScore DESC, so the lexical pool is 'the N freshest rows sharing any word with the query'. Widening the window (ftsOverfetch=4) and letting BM25 select in Kotlin was worth +0.011 on the scaffold.
  * vectorPoolSize ships DISABLED (0). It injects near-noise: a 384-dim hash sketch puts random unit vectors at |cos| ~= 1/sqrt(384) ~= 0.051. Re-enable only with a real embedder and a re-measurement — which is now possible and has not been done.
  * Raising the baseline in the same commit is the point of the gate. A future change that gives back a gain must fail rather than pass because the bar was left low.
